title: Resolve backlog amplification and uneven batching causing intermittent latency spikes
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Multiple enterprise customers (one Hosted, one Dedicated, and a Private VPC customer) reported intermittent 95th/99th percentile token latency spikes over the last two weeks. Spikes correlate with high long-context requests interleaving with small, low-latency requests. On-host traces show request queues growing for certain worker shards and then draining in large bursts leading to tail latency amplification. This ticket scopes investigation, short-term mitigations, and a long-term fix to the continuous batching and scheduler behavior that amplifies backlogs under mixed-length workloads.
symptoms_observed: Occasional 5-12x jump in token generation latency at 95/99 percentiles; CPU/GPU utilization remains within nominal range; queue depth telemetry shows per-shard queues accumulating while others are idle; KV cache evictions sometimes spike right before bursts. Customers saw increased request timeouts and a few production retries. No model correctness regressions observed.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a mixed workload: 30% long-context requests (>12k tokens), 70% short requests (<256 tokens) to a single model variant.
2) Configure batcher with continuous batching enabled, target_batch_size=1024, max_wait_ms=40.
3) Observe per-shard queue depth and token latency metrics for ~30 minutes; spikes appear once long requests interleave with small ones at ~10-15 minute intervals.
4) Attach tracer to scheduler to see batch assembly decisions; reproduce locally with synthetic traffic using load-generator script in linked artifacts.
root_cause_summary: A scheduler heuristic intended to maximize throughput biases batch formation toward older queued sequences but fails to account for mixed-length padding cost and KV cache eviction side effects. When a shard receives a burst of long-context requests, the continuous batcher pads many unrelated short requests into the same batch, causing substantial per-token compute cost and triggering KV cache pressure. This leads to eviction-induced cache misses for subsequent requests and creates cascading queue growth on affected shards. Additionally, the shard-affinity routing does not rebalance fast enough, so work remains imbalanced for multiple scheduling cycles.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 - Aisha V: Triage call with oncall and support. Collected logs from customer X (Hosted) and Y (Dedicated). Reproduced latency spike in internal staging with synthetic mixed workload.
2026-03-04 - Miguel S: Identified correlation between batch padding ratio and 99p spikes. Instrumented batcher to emit padding_ratio and per-request sequence_length_histogram.

2026-03-06 - Priya N (SRE): Short-term mitigation deployed: lowered continuous batch max_wait_ms from 40ms to 20ms for affected customers and enabled stricter per-shard inflight limits. Initial reduction in 99p observed (~40% improvement) for Hosted test cluster.

2026-03-08 - Miguel S: Root-cause narrowed to (a) padding amplification, (b) KV cache eviction spikes when many long-context batches execute consecutively, and (c) slow shard rebalancing. Drafted detailed fix plan and design doc.

2026-03-10 - Design review: Agreed on two-phase approach: immediate soft mitigation (dynamic batch heuristics + per-shard backpressure) and long-term scheduler rewrite to include sequence-length-aware batch scoring and faster shard rebalancing.

2026-03-12 - Feature branch open: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 - initial implementation of sequence-length-aware batch scoring and per-shard throttles. Running integration tests against staging.
2026-03-13 - Observability: New dashboard panels added for padding_ratio, per-shard_kv_evictions, and sequence_length_skew (dashboard link in artifacts).
mitigation_plan: Short-term (hotfix): Reduce max_wait_ms and add per-shard inflight request caps for affected pools; deploy via canary to 10% of traffic for Hosted customers and to a single Dedicated pool for verification.

Medium-term (next 2 sprints): Add sequence-length-aware scoring in batcher: prefer grouping similar-length requests, introduce max_padding_ratio threshold to reject grouping if exceeded, and delay long sequences slightly to avoid immediate mixing.
Long-term: Rewrite scheduler routing to implement proactive shard rebalancing based on sequence length heatmaps and implement KV cache stabilizers to avoid chained evictions during long-batch runs.
Operational: Add automated alerts for padding_ratio > 0.6 and per-shard_kv_evictions > baseline; update runbook for customer-facing mitigation steps.
Customer comms: Send interim report and mitigation summary to impacted customers; offer Dedicated customers an option to pin workloads to isolated pools as temporary relief.
testing_plan: Unit tests for batch scoring logic and padding ratio enforcement.
Deterministic integration tests using mixed-length synthetic workload (existing load generator) to assert no 99p regression.
End-to-end canary in staging with real tracing enabled, comparing old vs new scoring on the same traffic stream.
Chaos test: introduce KV cache thrash scenario to validate stabilizers prevent cascade evictions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy scoring change + per-shard throttles to 10% hosted traffic and one dedicated pool. Monitor 95/99p token latency, padding_ratio, and kv_evictions for 48 hours.
Phase 2 (gradual): If no regressions, increase to 50% over 6 hours, then 100% over next 24 hours for hosted; for dedicated/private, coordinate Maintenance windows with customers.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase >10% in 99p compared to baseline for more than 30 minutes or new errors >0.1% request rate.
open_questions: What target padding_ratio threshold balances latency vs throughput for low-P50 workloads?
Should Dedicated customers get a config toggle (sequence-length-aware batching) immediately or only as part of runtime-1.23?
Do we need a KV cache admission controller to protect hot cache lines during long-batch execution?
